claim: You can use your own domain name for a Transfer Family endpoint: the service supplies a domain name by default, and you can use Amazon Route 53 or any DNS service to route traffic from your registered domain to the server endpoint; the documentation on how AWS Transfer Family uses Amazon Route 53 for custom domain names applies to internet-facing endpoints only.

evidence.quote: Yes. The service supplies a domain name by default to access your endpoint. If you already have a domain name, you can use Amazon Route 53 or any DNS service to route your users’ traffic from your registered domain to the server endpoint in AWS. Refer to the documentation on how AWS Transfer Family uses Amazon Route 53 for custom domain names (applicable to internet facing endpoints only).
